questions.question: How does ViT (Vision Transformer) convert an image into a sequence for the transformer?
options: It processes each pixel individually
It splits the image into fixed-size patches, flattens and linearly projects each patch into a token embedding
It uses a CNN to extract feature maps then flattens them
It converts each row of pixels into a token
questions.explanation: ViT divides the image into 16×16 (or 32×32) patches. Each patch is flattened and projected to d_model via a linear layer, creating a sequence of patch tokens. A [CLS] token is prepended and positional embeddings are added before the standard transformer encoder.

questions.question: Why did early ViT models require large datasets (JFT-300M) to outperform CNNs?
options: Transformers are inherently slower than CNNs
CNNs have strong inductive biases (local connectivity, translation equivariance) that ViT lacks — ViT must learn these from data
ViT uses more parameters than CNNs
ViT cannot process color images
questions.explanation: CNNs encode translation equivariance and local feature extraction by design. ViT is a general sequence model with no spatial inductive bias — every patch can attend to every other from layer 1. This flexibility requires more data to learn the spatial structure CNNs get for free.

questions.question: What does DINO (Self-DIstillation with NO labels) demonstrate about ViT?
options: ViT can be compressed using knowledge distillation
ViT self-attention heads learn semantically meaningful object segmentation without any supervision
ViT can process video by treating frames as tokens
DINO replaces positional encoding with learned tokens
questions.explanation: DINO trained ViT with self-supervised learning showed that attention heads spontaneously learn to attend to object boundaries and semantically coherent regions — without any labels. This emergent segmentation property was unexpected and sparked major interest in ViT for dense prediction.

questions.question: What is the 'register token' technique introduced to improve ViT attention quality?
options: Additional CLS tokens for multi-label classification
Extra learned tokens added to the sequence that absorb 'background' attention, preventing artifacts in feature maps
Position tokens for absolute position encoding
Tokens that represent class labels
questions.explanation: Research found that certain patch tokens in ViT become 'attention sinks' — they absorb disproportionate attention and corrupt feature maps for dense tasks. Register tokens are additional learnable tokens that absorb this excess attention, dramatically improving attention map quality for segmentation.

questions.question: How does Swin Transformer address ViT's quadratic attention scaling for high-resolution images?
options: By using smaller patch sizes
By computing attention only within local windows that shift between layers to capture cross-window interactions
By applying strided convolutions before attention
By reducing the number of transformer layers
questions.explanation: Swin computes self-attention within fixed-size local windows (e.g., 7×7 patches), making complexity linear in image size. Windows shift between layers so cross-window connections are captured. Swin also introduces a hierarchical structure with patch merging, analogous to CNN feature pyramids.
